annotations.description: Jeskai Revelation is a 7-mana spell on the stack that will deal 4 damage, bounce a permanent, create two tokens, draw two cards, and gain 4 life. This is a massive swing spell that should be the target of the bounce effect itself. By choosing to bounce an opponent's Steam Vents (an untapped land), Kimi25 is allowing Jeskai Revelation to fully resolve - the opponent gets all the benefits (4 damage, 2 tokens, 2 cards, 4 life gain) while only losing a land temporarily. Bouncing the Jeskai Revelation spell itself would counter it entirely (returning it to the opponent's hand without any of its effects resolving), which is enormously better. Alternatively, Kimi25 has countermagic in hand (No More Lies, Spell Snare) but those can't counter a 7-mana spell effectively. Wait - actually, Kimi25 is the one being targeted by Jeskai Revelation and is selecting the target for the bounce effect. Looking more carefully: the opponent cast Jeskai Revelation, and Kimi25 is being asked to select the target for the 'return target spell or permanent to its owner's hand' part. Actually, re-reading: it says 'Select a spell or permanent' and one of the choices IS Jeskai Revelation itself. If Kimi25 bounces Jeskai Revelation back to the opponent's hand, the spell would be returned to hand and the rest of its effects would still resolve (since the spell is already on the stack resolving). So bouncing the spell itself doesn't fizzle it. However, bouncing Steam Vents is still a very low-value choice. Kimi25 could bounce their own Seam Rip to replay it later, or bounce the opponent's land. But the real question is: why didn't Kimi25 counter Jeskai Revelation with No More Lies (costs WU, opponent has 4 untapped lands but needs to pay 3 extra)? The opponent has Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, Island, and potentially one more untapped - they have exactly 4 untapped mana sources, so they could pay the 3. Actually looking at the board: Sonnet Vorthos has Steam Vents (untapped), Riverpyre Verge (untapped), Island (untapped) = 3 untapped lands, so they could pay exactly 3. So No More Lies wouldn't work. But bouncing a random land instead of something more impactful is still suboptimal. The real issue is the target choice - bouncing an opponent's untapped Steam Vents is nearly meaningless when they have plenty of other lands. Kimi25 should bounce their own Seam Rip (to replay it as a reusable removal spell) or even Cori Mountain Monastery for value.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to bounce opponent's Steam Vents (an untapped dual land) with Jeskai Revelation's bounce effect
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Kimi25's own Seam Rip to be able to replay it later as repeatable removal, or bounce a more impactful permanent. Bouncing a land when the opponent has 8 lands is nearly meaningless.

annotations.description: Kimi25 declined to counter Jeskai Revelation, a 7-mana spell that deals 4 damage, bounces a permanent, creates two tokens, draws two cards, and gains 4 life. This is an enormous swing card that represents a massive card advantage and tempo shift. Kimi25 had two copies of No More Lies in hand and 8 untapped lands available (the board shows several lands, enough to cast No More Lies for WU). The opponent at 13 life is casting this at 9 life Kimi25, meaning the 4 damage brings Kimi25 to 5 life while the opponent gains 4 life going to 17, creates two prowess tokens as threats, draws two cards, and bounces a Steam Vents. The life swing alone is 8 points, plus the card advantage and board presence. No More Lies would counter it unless the opponent pays 3, and the opponent has only 4 lands untapped (Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, Island, and one more) - wait, looking more carefully, the opponent has Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, Island untapped. That's 3 untapped lands, so the opponent could potentially pay the 3 mana for No More Lies. However, the opponent just cast a 7-mana spell, so they likely used most of their mana. Let me recount: opponent has 8 lands, Jeskai Revelation costs 7 (4URW), so they'd have 1 land untapped at most. They could NOT pay the additional 3 for No More Lies. This was a clear counter opportunity that would have exiled a devastating spell.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority and allowed Jeskai Revelation to resolve, taking 4 damage (going to 5 life), losing a Steam Vents to bounce, letting opponent create two Monk tokens, draw two cards, and gain 4 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Jeskai Revelation. The opponent spent 7 mana on it and would have at most 1 mana untapped, making it impossible to pay the additional 3. This would exile the Revelation and prevent an enormous swing in the opponent's favor.

annotations.actionTaken: Selected Stock Up and Three Steps Ahead from Consult the Star Charts
annotations.betterLine: Should have taken Restless Anchorage (win condition / free land drop) plus Three Steps Ahead. The deck desperately needs a way to actually win the game, not more card draw into more reactive spells.

annotations.description: Passed the main phase without casting Stock Up while opponent was completely tapped out. With 3 untapped lands (exactly enough for Stock Up's {2}{U} cost) and the opponent having zero mana available, this was a risk-free window to cast a sorcery. While Kimi25 already has 9 cards in hand (above hand size), the card selection from Stock Up (look at 5, keep 2) would help find win conditions they clearly need, since they appear to have no creatures on board. The reasoning about 'attacking' seems confused since Aang's Iceberg is an enchantment, not a creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the precombat main phase without casting any spells, seemingly to move to combat despite having no creatures to attack with.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Stock Up with the 3 available mana while opponent is tapped out, getting valuable card selection to find threats, then discard excess cards at end of turn.

annotations.description: Sacrificed Aang's Iceberg for scry 2, which returns whatever permanent it was exiling back to the opponent's battlefield, AND taps out all remaining mana so no countermagic (No More Lies x3, Spell Snare) can be held up. The opponent is at 5 life - maintaining control with countermagic is critical. Scry 2 is marginal when the hand already has 7 cards of interaction.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aang's Iceberg waterbend to sacrifice it for scry 2, tapping out remaining 3 mana
annotations.betterLine: Pass without activating, keeping 3 mana up to hold No More Lies as countermagic during the opponent's turn. The Iceberg continues exiling a threat while counter protection is maintained.
